summary.title: Building a Gas Pump Scanner with OpenCV/Python/iOS
summary.one_liner: You learn how one developer used OpenCV adaptive thresholding, contour filtering and k-NN digit classification in Python, then ported the pipeline to Objective-C++ for an iOS app that reads fuel pump digits from the camera.
keywords: how to read digits from an image
takeaways: Adaptive thresholding plus erosion and contour detection can isolate LCD digits from a photo of a gas pump, with aspect-ratio and alignment filters to discard non-digits.
Decimal points are found by checking small square contours within the span of the digits and the lower half of that span.
k-NN classification trained on labeled digit crops (folders 0-9) can be used with OpenCV, and the training data can be serialized to JSON for reuse on iOS.
Parameters were tuned manually with trackbars and then automatically by searching combinations over a labeled test set (about 7 hours of runtime).
Glare on the pump display and phone angle are the main failure cases; smoothing predictions over time reduces jitter when tapping a button.
summary.summary: The author describes building a prototype in Python with OpenCV to read digits from a gas pump image before porting it to an iOS app (FuelMate). The pipeline covers exposure adjustment, grayscale conversion, mild blur, adaptive Gaussian thresholding, erosion to close gaps in 7-segment digits, inverting colors, and findContours, followed by filtering contours by aspect ratio (about 0.6 for digits, 0.3 for '1') and height/vertical alignment. Digits are classified with OpenCV's k-NN, with training data exported to JSON for the C++ side, and parameters are tuned both manually and by automated search. The article is a high-level write-up that links to the GitHub code and does not provide a line-by-line code review.
